metadata.review_title: Excellent value! This can make more than just flowers, and the flowers it makes are great!

review_text:
I originally bought this after watching a great YouTube video on making gift card envelopes and other cards with this punch board. Then I started making flowers, and I am in love! This board isn't going to give you as much variety in flower type as other option (Cricut's 3D flower cartridges, for instance), but the flowers it make consistently look great and are very easy to assemble. I didn't bother spending money on WRMK's paper flower kits, which include stems, stamens, and pistils. Instead, I've made my own stems with various items, including wire wrapped to a chopstick with green washi tape.

For the flower centers, I discovered that 10mm glass cabochons are PERFECT center pieces for the XXS flower size. I attach them to paper flowers cut out with Fiskars' small and medium flower punches using a dot of Modge Podge dimensional magic. The final effect is really nice.

Hot glue works really well for piecing these together, especially if you start removing petals for a flower with a smaller diameter. I've also found that it works well to make a small circle of paper, cut a slit halfway into the circle, and make a shallow cone to wrap the back of the flower.

I'm really happy with this board. I think it has more to offer than Cricut's cartridges, because it's not DRMed, doesn't require a Cricut (or electricity at all!), and it can create lots of different things. Look on YouTube for how-tos on making cards with this punch board!

I added some photos to review to illustrate flowers, centers using glass cabochons and flower punches, paper cone flower backs, and the gift card holder you can make with this board.
This really is handy for dealing with small cut out items.

metadata.review_title: Goldfaber are Golden! Lovely to Work With.. Hopeful of More Colors to Come!

review_text:
Goldfaber are Golden! Watching tutorials (dangerous warning) I came across one on this great little set of Goldfaber Faber-Castell.. 48 count! I was very impressed! These pencils are simply beautiful as far presentation goes.. they are well made and the thickness is lovely to hold! They came in a nice, easy to open, hinged tin, with the expected plastic trays to hold pencils.. the only difference is the elastic on the sides (pic included) to lift out instead of the finger wedges to lift out.. I LOVED the elastic.. BRAVO Faber-Castell! It's much more stable in keeping pencils in the trays so they don't fall out and easier to lift out.. ESPECIALLY for those with arthritis like me!
In the tutorial (should you be interested in this info) it had stated that as far as Faber-Castell goes.. the red packaging is more for younger school age, the blue for more beginner, older students and the green (polychromos) for the more serious, professional artist.. which I'm not.. I'm a hobbyist & I LOVE to color.. so I couldn't wait to try these out.. next on my list is the Polychromos.. I've tried one just they cost a pretty penny!
I wasn't so keen on the red packaged Faber-Castell Pencils.. they were just ok but couldn't even compete with these Goldfabers! They worked beautifully with other pencils, blenders & mineral spirits. Little dust, very little if any wax bloom (I personally didn't get any but others have said they had), layered wonderfully.. GREAT value for your money.. my only con this far is the biggest set you can get is 48.. I do hope they add more to the Goldfaber Collection.. but to leave on a positive note, although the pencils don't have names, they do have numbers and can be replaced as needed with open stock availability.. YAY.. which isn't the case with most pencils!
UPDATE: I'm not going to take away stars since it could just be a defective tin.. and these pencils are lovely (I wish there was a larger set).. as I've been using my pencils and waiting for my pencil case to arrive I've noticed my tin doesn't stay shut very well.. no harm to my pencils but maybe don't depend on the tin so much. 😉

The WingKind double sided wash-away quilters tape is the best value for the price. It is every bit as fine quality as the name brand. The tape comes packaged in two (!) 22 yd rolls, has super adhesion, and, unlike other after market tapes, the plastic top stays stuck to the tape until you choose to remove it. I've had some where they separated long before I could get the tape pressed into place. The great adhesion allows me to use it successfully with vinyl and cork when making purses. It washes away, should it peek out anywhere, with a light application of water and a little rubbing with a terry cloth. I highly recommend this WingKind brand of 1/4" washable tape. You won't be sorry. Tip! Keep unused tape in a zip baggie so it doesn't dry out.
